title: Progressive traffic-shaping and attributable regression contracts for Optimize evals
creator: Ava Chen
description: PRD to define an evaluation and rollout contract that pairs automatic, measurable traffic shaping with cohort-attributable regression thresholds for Optimize. The goal is to enable safer model rollouts by: 1) defining per-cohort evaluation signal contracts (quality, latency, cost), 2) implementing an auto-throttle/traffic-shaping policy that scales traffic to a new model variant in proportion to observed risk, and 3) providing clear rollback and mitigation rules with attribution so product teams can act on root cause rather than noisy aggregate metrics.
scope: IN: tiered canary routing, auto-throttle algorithm, cohort attribution for primary signals (accuracy proxies, safety flags, latency p95, token-cost per request), A/B statistical test configuration for staged rollouts, runbook and alerting thresholds. OUT: automated model retraining, UI redesign for Console (only minimal dashboard widgets included), extended network isolation customizations for Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Define a deterministic contract document listing primary signals, cohort definitions, expected baselines, and allowed delta windows for first-, second-, and third-stage rollouts.

Auto-throttle behavior integrated into routing layer such that a newly-deployed variant can be scaled between 0% and 25% (stage 1), 25% and 60% (stage 2), and 60% and 100% (stage 3) based on severity score computed from live signals.
Attribution system returns per-cohort deltas with p-values and effect sizes for each primary signal within 15 minutes of traffic entering a new stage.

Runbook documents explicit rollback triggers: immediate rollback for high-severity safety regressions; staged throttle reduction for medium-severity accuracy or latency regressions; automated progressive rollback when severity persists for >30 minutes despite mitigation.
Dashboard shows live throttle factor, per-cohort delta heatmap, and causal tags (prompt cohort, customer tier, region) with links to the incident runbook and recent PRs.
End-to-end tests that simulate injected regressions and confirm the routing layer reduces traffic to the new variant according to the throttle policy in at least 95% of test runs.
Stakeholders (PM/ENG/RESEARCH/SRE) have signed off on the measurement definitions and the runbook.
Security review completed if the attribution pipeline needs access to customer PII — currently not required by scope.
rollout_plan: Stage 0: dry-run in canary with synthetic traffic and no customer-facing traffic (validation window: 4 hours).
Stage 1: progressive 0-25% traffic for 24 hours with auto-throttle enabled and 15-minute evaluation windows.
Stage 2: expand to 25-60% if no unresolved medium/high signals; monitor cohort deltas for 48 hours.
Stage 3: 60-100% final sweep with continued monitoring and 7-day elevated telemetry retention for Optimize-related signals.
monitoring_signals: Quality proxies: composite score of BLEU-like proxy, n-gram repetition, and user-rated correctness (where available).
Safety flags: count and rate of policy-triggered responses and triaged safety incidents.
Latency: p50/p95/p99 and tail variance for request completion time.
Cost: token-cost per request and per-customer spend delta vs baseline.
User friction: increase in follow-up clarification prompts and reduction in task completion rate (where instrumented).
rollback_triggers: Immediate rollback: any safety flag rate > 5x baseline OR any single safety incident that matches 'high-harm' severity (as defined in safety taxonomy).
Automated throttle reduction: composite severity score between 1.2x and 3x baseline sustained for >15 minutes causes throttle to be halved within the next evaluation window.
Stage pause and investigation: accuracy proxy degradation > 10% for critical cohorts OR latency p95 increase >100ms for >10% of requests in a stage triggers a Stage pause and paged alert to SRE/PM.

Auto-rollback: if a medium-severity condition persists after two automated mitigations (throttle reduction and parameter fallback) for >30 minutes, revert to previous pinned model variant automatically.
experiment_design: Use weighted-Bayes A/B testing per cohort with pre-specified hypothesis for each primary signal. Each stage uses independent hypothesis testing with a global alpha adjusted for sequential analyses. Cohorts include: top-10k prompts by volume, new-prompts (<30 days), premium-customer traffic, low-latency sensitive routes, and region-level cohorts. Attribution includes propensity weighting to adjust for routing differences introduced by throttling.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Tradeoffs: stricter contracts and aggressive throttle policies reduce customer exposure to regressions but slow rollouts and increase time-to-value. Attribution complexity adds latency to decisioning and may require additional compute. Risks: false positives on noisy cohorts could cause unnecessary rollbacks; incomplete cohort coverage could hide regressions in long-tail traffic. Mitigations: conservative default thresholds, synthetic test injection, and a manual override path for product owners.
notes: We intentionally require per-cohort attribution to avoid 'one-size-fits-all' rollbacks that penalize low-risk cohorts.
This PRD assumes runtime support for fractional routing and a signal ingestion pipeline that can return cohort deltas within 10-15 minutes.
If ENG-21111 (fast attribution index) slips, we will run an interim plan that uses coarser region-level attribution and a longer evaluation window (30m).
